LESSON: READING 10.2.1 INTENSIVE READING FACTUAL TEXTS OF ABOUT 400 WORDS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five
Subject: General
Strand: LEISURE TIME ACTIVITIES Suggested Vocabulary: leisure, interest, favourite, cine
Topic 10.2: Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading Factual Texts of about 400 Words
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading Factual Texts of about 400 Words, part of LEISURE TIME ACTIVITIES Suggested Vocabulary: leisure, interest, favourite, cine in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we read books? 2. Why should we make notes when reading? 3. What makes you a good reader?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. relate the ideas in a text to their experiences for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading Factual Texts of about 400 Words in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. respond to factual and inferential questions from a text correctly,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading Factual Texts of about 400 Words in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. summarise the main ideas in a text for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading Factual Texts of about 400 Words in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. encourage others to pay attention to detail when reading. Learner is guided to: • Skim through a text and obtain the main idea. • Scan through a text to obtain specific information. • Discuss and relate ideas to their experiences collaboratively with peers. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech/ digital devices with text- to-speech application or point/sign or write to express their views. • Read a text independently and retell it in own words. 1. Why do we read books? 2. Why should we make notes when reading? 3. What makes you a good reader? 87 • Answer direct and inferential questions from the text. • Watch a video on leisure time and write the main points. Learners with postural defects or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view. Screen resolution and light intensity could be regulated for learners who are sensitive to light.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading Factual Texts of about 400 Words together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.
